transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-16
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CSM) — Metronet: Carlos Rivera, Maya Chen, Ravi Patel, Sofia Martins

Summary (auto): QBR-style health check touching on usage, cost, reliability incidents, roadmap alignment, and security/compliance ask. Action items captured at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. quick roll call?
[00:05] Carlos Rivera: Hey Jordan, Carlos here. Maya and Ravi and Sofia on from our side.
[00:08] Maya Chen: Yep hi.
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll keep this to about 45, go over usage, cost, recent incidents, and then roadmap. Priya will jump in for technical bits.
[01:12] Priya Shah: cool, I've pulled the last 90 days of telemetry — saw a 3x spike in token volume since February, mostly due to the new chat assistant flows. average request size up ~25% which impacts cost.
[01:40] Maya Chen: yeah that's us, the new product launch increased multi-turn context, and we kept long history enabled.
[02:05] Jordan Lee: Understood. On cost — you're on hosted usage tier, correct?
[02:10] Carlos Rivera: yes, hosted. we've been eyeing Dedicated for predictable throughput but worried about commit sizes and price.
[02:25] Priya Shah: Tradeoff is predictability vs flexibility — Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity and consistent p99 latency, Hosted is pay as you go but can vary. Also Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization to reduce per-token cost.
[02:45] Sofia Martins: quick Q: we had two incidents in May where latency spiked for about 20-30 mins, can you speak to the root cause?
[03:00] Liam O'Connor: I can cover that — there was an autoscaler misconfig combined with a model rollout that hit a less-optimized kernel path, led to CPU pressure on the control plane and slow routing. we rolled back the rollout and applied the autoscale patch.
[03:25] Ravi Patel: Was any customer data exposed during that?
[03:30] Priya Shah: No, it was a performance regression only — no data leak. logs show increased retry rates and some timeouts. we've added more aggressive fallback to a smaller model and improved circuit-breaking.
[04:05] Carlos Rivera: ok good. On security, Ravi wants to confirm we meet SOC 2 needs and KMS options for key management.
[04:15] Jordan Lee: We have SOC 2 Type II and can support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for Private offerings; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and rotation — will share the docs.
[04:38] Ravi Patel: We need audit logs and SSO/SAML + RBAC. Also data residency — currently our users are EU-heavy so we need EU data residency for logs and model usage records.
[04:55] Priya Shah: We can route requests to EU regions and keep metadata in-region for Private, and for Dedicated we can ensure cluster placement. I'll capture exact config options.
[05:20] Maya Chen: Back to costs — can you show quick numbers on where the spend is coming from? tokens vs embeddings vs overage?
[05:30] Jordan Lee: Looking at your account, 72% token generation, 18% embeddings for search, 10% misc. Key drivers: average context length, not using KV caching for repeated prefixes, and no quant profiles applied to these model versions.
[05:55] Priya Shah: For a quick example: enabling prefix KV cache for the assistant cut token usage 12-18% in similar customers. Quantizing model to int8-like profile can reduce cost by another 20-30% but needs QA on output quality.
[06:20] Carlos Rivera: Can you run a benchmark comparing Hosted vs Dedicated for our load? latency p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens?
[06:34] Priya Shah: Yes; we'll run a small benchmark — replicate a 1k request sample and then scale out. note: Dedicated often gives better p95/p99 for steady loads.
[07:02] Sofia Martins: timeline — we have compliance review with procurement on 7/6 so need the security packet before then.
[07:12] Jordan Lee: we'll get SOC2 and KMS notes to you by 6/17.
[07:20] Ravi Patel: also need retention policy details — how long do you keep raw logs and can we set retention?
[07:30] Liam O'Connor: We retain platform logs 90 days by default, can extend on enterprise packages; we can also provide filtered exports. we'll include options in the doc.
[08:05] Maya Chen: On roadmap, we're planning multi-region failover and fine-grained rollout control — how does Redwood support canary and A/B model rollouts?
[08:20] Priya Shah: Redwood Console supports canary percentage rollouts, A/B via route configs, and automatic fallback policies if error rates spike. We also surface per-route latency and token cost breakdowns.
[08:50] Carlos Rivera: Any gotchas for switching from Hosted to Dedicated mid-quarter?
[08:58] Jordan Lee: The main items are commit sizing and model variants — you'll need to pin model versions for Dedicated; we can support seamless traffic shifting but there's planning needed for autoscale and capacity burst options.
[09:22] Maya Chen: We saw some transcripts where the ASR replaced KV cache with KV cash, minor but funny — just expect transcription artifacts :)
[09:35] Priya Shah: (laughs) yes the ASR does that.
[10:00] Carlos Rivera: SLA questions: what is the guaranteed uptime and latency SLOs?
[10:08] Jordan Lee: Hosted SLA is 99.9 availability for API; Dedicated has SLA with stricter latency targets for reserved instances depending on commit tier. We'll put exact numbers in the pricing doc.
[10:40] Ravi Patel: For encryption at rest — we need to know where keys reside and if we can bring our own key material.
[10:48] Jordan Lee: For Private and Dedicated you can bring your own key material via KMS/HSM. Hosted supports customer managed keys through an envelope schema with partner KMS providers.
[11:20] Sofia Martins: What about cost optimization tools — Redwood Optimize you mentioned, can it run as a service or is it advisory?
[11:30] Priya Shah: It's both: recommendations engine in Console that suggests batching, cache, and quantization profiles; we also offer implementation help as a paid engagement to apply safe quant profiles and validate outputs.
[12:05] Carlos Rivera: Let's talk concrete numbers — if we reduce average context length by 20% and enable KV cache for 60% of requests, what's the expected cost delta?
[12:20] Jordan Lee: Back-of-envelope: 20% shorter context reduces token spend proportionally, so ~20% headroom; KV cache for 60% requests cuts generation tokens for those by ~40% typically. Combined you'd see ~40-45% reduction overall depending on request shapes. We'll run a modeled scenario and send exact numbers.
[13:10] Maya Chen: For the benchmark, we'll provide 3 canonical prompt sets: support assistant long context, search embedding small contexts, and batch rerank.
[13:25] Priya Shah: perfect — please upload them to the shared drive link (we'll send) so we can reproduce.
[14:00] Jordan Lee: Quick note on model variants: if you plan to quantize, we recommend keeping a production baseline and a quantized variant to A/B test for quality.
[14:18] Carlos Rivera: On reliability, any recommended failover pattern to avoid the 30m spike we had?
[14:28] Priya Shah: yes — aggressive circuit breakers on the client, route policy to fallback to smaller model variant, and local prefix caching. We'll provide client-side SDK patterns.
[15:05] Ravi Patel: Are there any compliance gaps we should be aware of for EU residency?
[15:12] Liam O'Connor: For Hosted some metadata still flows through control plane in default US region; for full in-region residency we recommend Dedicated in-EU or Private install. We'll map the options by region.
[16:00] Sofia Martins: Ok great. Anything else on roadmap alignment?
[16:10] Maya Chen: we want to prioritize burst capacity for Black Friday-style events; how does Dedicated handle bursts?
[16:20] Priya Shah: Dedicated supports burst capacity options that allow short-term overcommit; there is an overage pricing model. We'll include examples.
[17:05] Jordan Lee: Recap & next steps: send pricing + cost scenarios, security docs, run benchmark, customer to provide prompt sets and traffic pattern.
[17:20] Carlos Rivera: Sounds good. Thank you.
[17:25] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and schedule the bench.
[17:30] End of meeting.
